cards.claim: Critical batch size (CBS) scales primarily with data size rather than model size
cards.conditions: Transformer language models (85M–1.2B parameters), C4 dataset, Adam optimizer, Chinchilla-optimal and controlled training settings
cards.effect: When data size is held constant and model size increases, CBS remains nearly invariant; when model size is constant and data size increases, CBS increases proportionally
cards.evidence: Controlled experiments comparing CBS across different model and data size combinations; power-law fitting of CBS vs. model size and data size
cards.quote: CBS weakly depends on model size but more strongly depends on data size

cards.claim: Exponential Weight Averaging (EWA) improves training efficiency at large batch sizes and enables training beyond fixed durations
cards.conditions: Large-scale language model pre-training with Adam optimizer, variable batch sizes, target-loss-based training (not fixed token budgets)
cards.effect: EWA achieves competitive performance with cosine and warmup-stable-decay schedules while eliminating the need to predefine training duration; improves optimization efficiency in large-batch regimes
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison of learning rate schedulers (constant+EWA, cosine, WSD, schedule-free) on model sizes 85M–1.2B
cards.quote: EWA can trade memory for optimization efficiency in LM pre-training, especially in large-batch regimes. This is useful in scenarios where a target loss must be achieved, but practitioners are uncertain of the exact maximum data size to set up the learning rate schedule for training.

cards.claim: Proper tuning of momentum and learning rate is essential when scaling batch size
cards.conditions: Language model pre-training on C4 dataset with Adam optimizer, batch size sweeps from 256 to 4096
cards.effect: Without proper hyperparameter sweeps, training efficiency gains from larger batches are lost; requires careful tuning of both momentum and learning rate per batch size
cards.evidence: Empirical ablation studies and appendix discussions of optimizer configuration sensitivity
cards.quote: ensuring proper sweeps of momentum and learning rate ... adopting well-tuned values for the parameter and the exponential weight averaging decay rate, tailored to each batch size

cards.claim: In infinite-width limit, critical batch size remains invariant when scaling model width, but this does not imply invariance for practical finite-width networks
cards.conditions: Neural networks with infinite-width initialization, fixed data size, fixed training duration, networks satisfying maximal update parameterization (muP)
cards.effect: Theoretical prediction that CBS should not scale with model width beyond some finite width; practical finite-width networks still exhibit width-dependent behavior
cards.evidence: Theorem 2 on infinite-width limits combined with empirical observation that practical networks (85M–1.2B) show weak dependence of CBS on model size
cards.quote: for fixed training tokens, we would expect that the critical batch size won't scale with model width beyond a point

cards.claim: Critical batch size in mini-batch SGD scales with data size according to power-law depending on source and capacity conditions
cards.conditions: Mini-batch SGD on well-specified Gaussian linear regression, fixed model size, varying data size, variance-dominated regime
cards.effect: In variance-dominated regime (as data size increases), CBS grows as a power law of data size; optimal learning rate and batch size must be rescaled jointly to maintain efficiency
cards.evidence: Corollary 2 (theoretical analysis of mini-batch SGD on least-squares problems with capacity/source conditions)
cards.quote: the CBS is ..., which (along with ...) allows mini-batch SGD output to attain the optimal rate of the expected excess risk (as data size grows) with the smallest number of steps

cards.claim: Learning rate scheduling strategies that require predefined total training duration become problematic when training beyond fixed durations to reach a target loss
cards.conditions: Language model pre-training without fixed token budget; goal is to reach specific target validation loss
cards.effect: Cosine decay and warmup-stable-decay schedules require careful tuning of decay duration; constant+EWA avoids this requirement while maintaining comparable efficiency
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison of scheduler variants (Figure 2) showing schedule-free and constant+EWA approaches perform comparably to tuned cosine schedules
cards.quote: learning rate decay strategies typically require predefining the total training duration ... To address this, we propose using exponential weight averaging (EWA) ... enabling training beyond fixed durations
